notes: ACCESS ROUTE: The assigned URL www.vtwonen.nl/shop is a DPG Media-owned editorial/media site whose /shop path is gated by DPG Media's own privacy-consent wall (myprivacy.dpgmedia.nl) that requires client-side JS acceptance and could not be bypassed via curl_cffi (11-profile sweep all landed on the consent redirect), r.jina.ai (Cloudflare-challenged under contention), or translate.goog (blocked by the same origin WAF). Investigation (WebSearch) showed vtwonen's actual webshop is operated on a separate subdomain, shop.vtwonen.nl -- confirmed by a third-party listing calling it 'vtwonen by fonQ' (Belgian sibling shop.vtwonen.be uses identical branding). curl_cffi impersonate=chrome124 reached shop.vtwonen.nl directly with HTTP 200, no consent gate, no WAF block. Footer copyright confirms '(c) 2026 DPG Media B.V.' with a real KVK company-registration link -- genuine, non-scam operator (Rule 3 sanity check passed), platform is Shopify (myshopify.com references, Shopify.shop/Shopify.theme JS, standard /collections/<handle>/products.json + sitemap_products_N.xml). robots.txt on both www.vtwonen.nl and shop.vtwonen.nl checked: generic 'Allow: /' with only /search and /feed disallowed for User-agent: * -- no ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai/Claude-Web disallow found, so proceeding was permitted. RELATED-COMPANY NOTE (not explicitly flagged in brief but discovered during work): this batch's S.N. 121 fonQ (fonq.nl) is very likely the same underlying platform/operator group as this vtwonen webshop (whitelabel arrangement, 'vtwonen by fonQ'); c121.json had not been written yet at extraction time so a direct catalogue/store-ID cross-check with fonQ was not possible from this worker -- flagged for orchestrator-level cross-check at merge. QTY METHOD (Rule 1): Shopify collection product_count/collections.json metafields were NOT used (project has proven these unreliable 6/6 elsewhere). Instead every qty was obtained by enumerating https://shop.vtwonen.nl/collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250&page=N to exhaustion (stopping when a page returns fewer than 250 unique product IDs, i.e. true last page reached, confirming the total is exact, not capped) -- this is one of Rule 1's explicitly approved cheap proofs ('enumerate to exhaustion and count unique product IDs'). Every leaf row's evidence records the pages fetched and final page size. ROLLUP/PARENT DECISIONS: 'verlichting' (top indoor-lighting collection, 7215) sums to ~95% of its 7 nav-linked lamp-type children (6848) -> treated as a pure rollup: dropped as its own row, kept only as the 'Indoor Lighting' parent grouping with the 7 children as leaves (matches project's established Blu Dot rollup precedent). 'glazen' (371) sums EXACTLY to all glass sub-types including 4 nav-linked ones (332, 89.5%) plus several untracked ones with no own URL (longdrink/tea/coffee/borrel/whiskey/cognac/beer glasses, 39 items, 10.5%, not separately extractable) -> treated as a pure rollup 'Glasses' parent, kept only the 4 nav-linked children. 'potterie' (575) sums EXACTLY to bloempotten(503)+plantenbakken(60)+potaccessoires(12, a minor functional pot-saucer/accessory line not separately extracted) -> treated as pure rollup 'Pots & Planters' parent with 2 children. By contrast: 'servies' (2025) is only 61% explained by its 2 nav-linked children (borden 571 + kopjes-mokken 666 = 1237); the other 39% (kommen/bowls 426, serveerschalen 154, amuseservies 130, serviessets 43, eierdopjes 19, kinderservies 16) have no dedicated collection URL of their own. 'buitenverlichting' (296, outdoor lighting) shares ZERO product-ID overlap with its only nav-listed child 'grondspot' (10) -- confirmed via ID-set intersection -- so grondspot is NOT actually nested inside buitenverlichting despite appearing in the same mega-menu column. 'buitenlampen' (185, a SEPARATE outdoor/garden-lighting collection under the Tuin nav, zero product-ID overlap with buitenverlichting) is however an exact rollup of Sfeerverlichting(127)+Sokkellampen(48)+Grondspot(10) by internal product_type tag, and grondspot IS a full 10/10 ID subset of buitenlampen. In all these low-coverage cases (servies, buitenverlichting, buitenlampen/grondspot) the broader category was KEPT as its own leaf (real distinct URL, real verified qty) rather than dropped, because dropping would have made large, genuinely-decorative populations (426 bowls, ~110 outdoor ambiance/pedestal lights, etc.) invisible with no other row representing them; the narrower nav-linked children were ALSO kept as separate leaves with the parent/child qty overlap explicitly documented here, per the project's general 'a documented overlap beats a missing category' principle (Rule 0.6), applied by extension beyond its literal room-vs-type scope. 'wanddecoratie' (wall-decor umbrella, capped at >=7500 during enumeration) product-type-sampled as ~88% Posters+Schilderijen (already extracted individually as their own nav-linked collections) plus several small untracked sub-types (fotowanden, wandpanelen, muurstickers, wandcirkels, wandkleden, decoratieve dierenhoofden, prenten, tekstborden/spreuktegels) with no dedicated collection URLs -- treated as a superset/mixed-rollup of two already-kept rows (Nordstrom 'Decorative Accents' precedent) and DROPPED entirely rather than double-counted or padded. RULE 0 GAINS: included baby-verlichting (nursery lighting, 16 -- night lamps/wall lamps for kids' rooms, genuine lighting fixtures) and baby-muurdecoratie (nursery wall decor, 6 -- wool/felt wall hangings) purely on product-type grounds despite the 'baby' room-word, exactly per Rule 0's instruction that room words never disqualify a qualifying product type; also kept buitenverlichting/buitenlampen/grondspot (outdoor lighting, Rule 0.1/0.5) as full leaf rows rather than excluding for being outdoor. EXCLUDED categories and why (spot-checked actual product titles/product_type before excluding, per project rule): geurstokjes (114, reed diffusers = home fragrance); koffietafelboeken (70, coffee-table books, not a decor product type this project extracts); vloerkleden (4690, rugs = textile); wandplanken-en-rekken (209, spot-check showed floating/book/kitchen wall shelving units = functional storage furniture, not decorative wall art); koffie-en-theeaccessoires (276, spot-check showed teapots/creamers mixed with barista machines, knock-boxes and tea strainers = mixed functional kitchen tools, dropped as an unclean mixed roll-up); badkamer-accessoires (313, spot-check showed towel/toothbrush/soap/toilet-roll holders, toilet brushes, makeup organisers = bathroom hardware/utility, Rule 0.4 exclusion; the single 'Scheerspiegels' shaving-mirror sub-type found was 1 item, too negligible to extract separately); tuindecoratie (192, spot-check showed a genuine mix of outdoor wall canvas/garden posters alongside cooler boxes and a wooden rose arch with no separable sub-URL -- dropped as an unclean mixed bag); bloemen-planten/buitenplanten/zijden-boeketten (897/0/15, real and artificial flowers & plants, excluded per the faux-plant rule, buitenplanten is currently an empty collection); all furniture, bedding, textiles (kussens, beddengoed, vloerkleden, woontextiel, badtextiel), cleaning/laundry, garden furniture/BBQ, baby/kids furniture and toys, wallpaper/paint, door hardware and light-switch hardware, and all 'merk-*'/'shop-*' brand-storefront and sale/new-in/populair marketing collections were excluded outright as out of scope or non-category navigation per the brief.
